source_text: πρὸς πάντας, ἐν πραότητι διδάσκοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους.» Τὸ δὲ δεῖν ἕπεσθαι τοῖς ἤδη προειρημένοις καὶ τὴν αἰγὸς προσφορὰν, ἐκδείξειεν ἂν οὐχὶ ἕτερον, οἶμαι, τὶ, πλὴν ὅπερ ἔναγχος ἔφην, τὸ δεῖσθαι δὴ πάντας, κἂν εἴ τινες εἶεν ἀγαθοὶ τὴν ἕξιν, τοῦ διὰ μεταγνώσεως καθαρισμοῦ καὶ ἀμνηστίας παραπτωμάτων. Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδὼς ὁ θεῖος ἔφη Δαβίδ «Ἐὰν ἀνομίας παρατηρήσῃς, Κύριε, Κύριε, τίς ὑποστήσεται;» Χίμαρος δὴ οὖν τὸ ὑπὲρ ἀφέσεως θῦμα, κατὰ τὸν πάλαι νόμον. Μετάγνωσις δὲ νυνὶ καὶ ἀμνηστίας αἴτησις τὸ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἱερεῖον, τοὺς ἐν πνεύματί τε καὶ ἀληθείᾳ προσιόντας Θεῷ. «Λέγε γὰρ, φησὶ, σὺ τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου πρῶτος, ἵνα δικαιωθῇς.» Ψάλλει δέ που καὶ ὁ Δαβίδ· «Εἶπα, Ἐξαγορεύσω κατ' ἐμοῦ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν μου τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ σὺ ἀφῆκας τὴν ἀσέβειαν τῆς καρδίας μου.» Ἆρά σοι λοιπὸν σαφὴς ὁ λόγος περὶ τῆς τῶν ἀρχόντων δωροφορίας; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Χρῆναι δὲ οἶμαι κἀκεῖνο εἰπεῖν, προσκεκομισμένης γὰρ ἤδη τῆς παρ' ἑκάστου καὶ ὡς ὑπὲρ πάντων θυσίας, ἀρχὴ τῶν θείων ἐγένετο λόγων ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ πρὸς τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωσέα. Γέγραπται δὲ οὕτω πάλιν ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς· «Αὕτη ἡ ἐγκαίνισις τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, μετὰ τὸ πληρῶσαι τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τὸ χρίσαι αὐτόν. Ἐν τῷ εἰσπορεύεσθαι Μωσῆν εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, τοῦ λαλῆσαι αὐτῷ, καὶ ἤκουσε τὴν φωνὴν Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ λαλοῦντος πρὸς αὐτὸν ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου, ὅ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν δύο Χερουβὶμ, καὶ ἐλάλει πρὸς αὐτόν.» Τετελειωμένης γὰρ ὥσπερ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, καὶ ἀναδειχθέντος κόσμῳ τοῦ ἀληθοῦς ἁγιάσματος, ὅ ἐστιν ἡ Ἐκκλησία, τότε δὴ τότε φωνὴ γέγονε πρὸς ἡμᾶς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός. «Λελάληκε γὰρ ἡμῖν ἐν Υἱῷ,» ὃν καὶ ἱλαστήριον εἶναί φαμεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Ἄνωθεν δὲ τῶν Χερουβὶμ ἡ φωνή· κτίσεως γὰρ ἀνωτάτω καὶ ἐπέκεινα Θεὸς, οὐσιώδη τε καὶ ἐνυπάρχουσαν τὴν κατὰ παντὸς τοῦ γεγονότος ἔχων ὑπεροχήν· διαπορθμεύων δὲ εἰς ἡμᾶς τὰς ἄνωθεν καὶ παρὰ Πατρὸς φωνὰς, ἔφασκεν ὁ Υἱὸς, τὸ ἀληθὲς ἱλαστήριον, «Τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὰ, ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με.» Οὐκοῦν ἄνωθεν τοῦ ἱλαστηρίου γέγονεν ἡ φωνή. Θαυμάσαις δ' ἂν οὐ μετρίως τὴν τῶν φυλάρχων ἀνασκοπούμενος πρόσοδον. Ἀπονεμηθείσης γὰρ ἡμέρας ἑκάστῳ καὶ ἰδικῶς, καθ' ἣν ἔδει πληροῦν τὰ συντεταγμένα καὶ προσκομίσαι τὸ δῶρον, προσίεσαν μὲν ἐν κόσμῳ κατά γε τὸ τῷ νομοθέτῃ δοκοῦν· πλὴν οὐ κατὰ τὴν τῆς γενέσεως τάξιν, ἤτοι καθ' ἡλικίαν, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἀναμὶξ καὶ χύδην ἁπλῶς, συντεθειμένοι δὲ μᾶλλον ὥσπερ εἰς οἰκονομίαν μυστικήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μὴν ὅ τι ποτέ ἐστιν ὃ φὴς, ἐννοεῖν οὐκ ἔχω. Φράζε δὴ οὖν μοι σαφῶς. {ΚΥΡ.} Βούλει λέγωμεν ἐν τάξει καὶ καθεξῆς τοὺς ἐξ
pass_a_gloss: [completing the quotation begun in §35] toward all (πρὸς πάντας), in meekness (πραότης) teaching those who oppose (ἀντιδιατίθεμαι).’ And that the offering (προσφορά) of a goat (αἴξ) must follow (ἕπομαι) the things already said would show nothing else, I think, except what I said just now (ἔναγχος): that all need (δέομαι), even if some should be good in habit (ἕξις), the cleansing (καθαρισμός) through repentance (μετάγνωσις) and amnesty (ἀμνηστία) of trespasses (παραπτώματα). And knowing this the divine David said: ‘If you watch closely (παρατηρέω) iniquities (ἀνομίαι), Lord, Lord, who will withstand (ὑφίσταμαι)?’ So then the he-goat (χίμαρος) is the victim (θῦμα) for forgiveness (ἄφεσις) according to the old law; but now repentance and request (αἴτησις) of amnesty is the sacrifice (ἱερεῖον) in our case, [us] who approach God in spirit and truth. ‘For speak (λέγε) you your sins first, that you may be justified (δικαιόω),’ he says. And David sings somewhere: ‘I said, I will declare out (ἐξαγορεύω) against myself my sin to the Lord, and you forgave (ἀφίημι) the impiety (ἀσέβεια) of my heart.’ Is then the account (λόγος) about the gift-bringing (δωροφορία) of the rulers (ἄρχοντες) clear to you now? PALL.: Wholly so. CYR.: And I think one must say that too: for when the sacrifice from each and as for all had already been brought, a beginning (ἀρχή) of the divine words (λόγοι) came to be in the holy tent toward the hierophant (ἱεροφάντης) Moses. And it is written thus again in Numbers: ‘This is the dedication (ἐγκαίνισις) of the altar (θυσιαστήριον), after filling his hands (πληρῶσαι τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ), and after anointing (χρίω) him. When Moses was going in (εἰσπορεύομαι) into the tent of testimony (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) to speak with him, he also heard the voice of the Lord God speaking to him from above the mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον), which is on the ark of the testimony (κιβωτὸς τοῦ μαρτυρίου), between the two cherubim, and he was speaking to him.’ For when the holy tent was as it were perfected (τελειόω), and the true sanctuary (ἁγίασμα) shown forth (ἀναδείκνυμι) to the world, which is the Church, then, then indeed (τότε δὴ τότε) the voice of the God and Father came to us. ‘For he has spoken to us in a Son,’ whom we also say is the mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον) for our sins, according to the Scriptures. And the voice is from above the cherubim; for God is highest above and beyond creation (κτίσις), having the supremacy (ὑπεροχή) over all that has come to be as essential (οὐσιώδης) and inherent (ἐνυπάρχουσα). And ferrying across (διαπορθμεύω) to us the voices from above and from the Father, the Son, the true mercy seat, said: ‘The words (ῥήματα) that I speak are not mine, but of him who sent me.’ So the voice came from above the mercy seat. And you would marvel not moderately, examining (ἀνασκοπέω) the approach (πρόσοδος) of the tribe-leaders (φύλαρχοι). For a day having been allotted to each also individually (ἰδικῶς), on which he had to fulfil the things arranged (συντεταγμένα) and bring the gift, they approached in order (ἐν κόσμῳ) according to what seemed good to the lawgiver (νομοθέτης); except not according to the order (τάξις) of birth (γένεσις), that is by age (ἡλικία), nor mixed up and in a heap (ἀναμὶξ καὶ χύδην) simply, but rather arranged as it were into a mystical economy (οἰκονομία μυστική). PALL.: And yet whatever it is you say, I am not able to understand. So explain (φράζω) to me clearly. CYR.: Do you wish we should say in order and successively those born of… [continues in §37: ‘Jacob’]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …toward all, teaching with meekness those who oppose him’ (2 Timothy 2:24–25). That the offering of a goat must follow what has already been named (Numbers 7:16) would show, I think, nothing other than what I said just now: that all people, even any whose settled character is good, need cleansing through repentance and the pardon of their trespasses. Knowing this, the divine David said: ‘If you should mark iniquities, Lord, Lord, who will stand?’ (Psalm 130:3). Under the old law, then, the goat was the sacrifice for forgiveness. But now repentance and the plea for pardon are the sacrifice for us who draw near to God in spirit and in truth (John 4:23). For it says: ‘State your sins first, that you may be justified’ (Isaiah 43:26). And David too sings somewhere: ‘I said, I will confess my sin against myself to the Lord, and you forgave the ungodliness of my heart’ (Psalm 32:5). Is the account of the leaders’ gifts clear to you now?

Cyril: I think this too must be said. For when the sacrifice had already been brought by each, and as it were on behalf of all, the divine words began to come to Moses, the revealer of the sacred rites, in the holy tent. It is written thus, again in Numbers: ‘This is the dedication of the altar, after his hands were filled and after he was anointed. When Moses went into the tent of testimony to speak with him, he heard the voice of the Lord God speaking to him from above the mercy seat, which is on the ark of the testimony, between the two cherubim; and he spoke to him’ (Numbers 7:88–89). For when the holy tent had, as it were, been completed, and the true sanctuary, which is the Church, had been shown to the world, then indeed the voice of God the Father came to us. ‘For he has spoken to us in the Son’ (Hebrews 1:2), whom we also call the mercy seat for our sins, according to the Scriptures (Romans 3:25; 1 John 2:2). The voice comes from above the cherubim, for God is above all creation and beyond it, and his supremacy over everything that has come into being belongs to his very essence and is inherent in him. And the Son, the true mercy seat, conveying to us the words that come from above and from the Father, said: ‘The words that I speak are not mine, but his who sent me’ (John 14:10, 24). So the voice came from above the mercy seat. You would also marvel not a little as you consider the approach of the tribal leaders. For a day was assigned to each one separately (Numbers 7:11), on which he was to carry out what had been prescribed and bring his gift. They came forward in good order, as the lawgiver decided; yet not in the order of their birth, that is, by age, nor simply mixed together at random, but arranged instead, as it were, in a mystical order.
Palladius: And yet I cannot work out what you mean. So tell me plainly.
Cyril: Would you like us to name, in order and one after another, those born of…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation, completing 2 Timothy 2:24–25 begun at the end of §35. Cyril’s text skips ‘apt to teach, patient’ (διδακτικόν, ἀνεξίκακον) between 2:24 and 2:25; the gap is his, not the translator’s. The goat ‘for sin’ is Numbers 7:16; Cyril uses both αἴξ and χίμαρος for it. Psalm 130:3 = LXX Psalm 129:3 (‘ἐὰν ἀνομίας παρατηρήσῃς, κύριε, κύριε, τίς ὑποστήσεται’). Isaiah 43:26 LXX (‘λέγε σὺ τὰς ἀνομίας σου πρῶτος, ἵνα δικαιωθῇς’), which the Hebrew-based English Bibles render differently; Cyril has ἁμαρτίας for ἀνομίας. Psalm 32:5 = LXX Psalm 31:5; Cyril has ἁμαρτίαν where the LXX has ἀνομίαν in the second clause. ‘In spirit and in truth’ cited to John 4:23 because it is the Gospel phrase that names the whole work. Numbers 7:88–89: the quotation starts at the last clause of 7:88 (‘This is the dedication of the altar…’) and runs through 7:89; LXX ‘μετὰ τὸ πληρῶσαι τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ καὶ μετὰ τὸ χρῖσαι αὐτόν’ is ambiguous (the masculine pronouns do not agree with the neuter θυσιαστήριον; Hebrew has ‘after it was anointed’), so Pass B keeps ‘his hands… he was anointed’ as the Greek stands. ἱεροφάντης rendered ‘who revealed the sacred rites’ to avoid the pagan term ‘hierophant’. ἱλαστήριον rendered ‘mercy seat’ throughout so the type stays visible; ‘the mercy seat for our sins, according to the Scriptures’ cited to Romans 3:25 (Christ as ἱλαστήριον) and 1 John 2:2 (‘for our sins’). John 14:24: Cyril’s wording blends John 14:24 (‘the word you hear is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me’) with John 14:10 (‘the words that I speak to you’); cf. John 7:16; (reviewer) the opening ‘τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λαλῶ’ is John 14:10 and the close ‘τοῦ πέμψαντός με’ is John 14:24, so both are cited. ‘A day was assigned to each’ cited to Numbers 7:11 (‘one leader each day’). ‘The lawgiver’ (νομοθέτης) may mean God or Moses; left as Cyril has it. ‘Οἰκονομίαν μυστικήν’ rendered ‘a mystical order’. Section ends mid-sentence; §37 begins with ‘Ἰακὼβ’, so the English ends ‘those born of…’ and §37 opens ‘…Jacob?’
